chunks: As for what Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl, from some of our companions, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, he said:

Regarding a man who is performing tawaf and then a need arises for him, he said: there is no harm in his going to attend to his own need or the need of someone else and cutting off the tawaf. And if he wants to rest and sit, there is no harm in that. Then when he returns, he resumes his tawaf. If it is a supererogatory tawaf, he may resume after one circuit or two circuits; but if it is an obligatory tawaf, then if he went out for a need with another man, he does not resume from where he left off.

And not even in his own need. So this is not contrary to what we have mentioned, because what he meant by saying, 'he does not resume,' is that he does not resume after one circuit or two circuits, distinguishing between obligatory tawaf and supererogatory tawaf as we have explained. Do you not see that he said at the beginning of the report, 'there is no harm in that; then when he returns, he resumes his tawaf'? Then he began a ruling specific to supererogatory tawaf, which is the permissibility of resuming when less than half has been completed. Then he followed that by his saying, 'and if it is in an obligatory tawaf, he does not resume,' meaning what was permitted for him in the supererogatory tawaf. And that is not contrary to what we have said.

key_terms.الطَّوَافَ: tawaf, the ritual circumambulation around the Ka'bah
key_terms.الْحَاجَةُ: a need or matter requiring attention
key_terms.فَرِيضَةٍ: obligatory, referring to a required act of worship
key_terms.نَافِلَةً: supererogatory, referring to a non-obligatory devotional act
key_terms.يَبْنِي: he resumes or builds upon what he had already completed

ai.seo_question: Can a person interrupt tawaf for a need and then continue from where he left off?
ai.summary: This report discusses the legal ruling of interrupting tawaf because of a need, rest, or another matter. It distinguishes between obligatory tawaf and supererogatory tawaf, explaining that resumption is allowed in both generally, but the special allowance to build upon one or two circuits applies to supererogatory tawaf and not obligatory tawaf.
